test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 27 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 2, 15 and 10 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do twice the same work, working together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total original work = LCM(2, 15, 10) = 30 units.

Combined efficiency = (30 ÷ 2) + (30 ÷ 15) + (30 ÷ 10) = 15 + 2 + 3 = 20 units/day.

Twice the total work = 2 × 30 = 60 units.

Required time = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 2 days

Time taken by B = 15 days

Time taken by C = 10 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of all given days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Number of Days

Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of A, B and C = 15 + 2 + 3 = 20 units/day.

⇒ Target work to be completed = 2 × Original Total Work

⇒ Target work = 2 × 30 = 60 units.

⇒ Time taken = Target Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

This topic follows the exact same logic as Time and Work, with the key difference that emptying pipes or leakages are assigned a negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done by each person. If all individuals work together for the exact same duration, the wages can simply be distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

To solve these questions, group the work into cycles (e.g., A works on Day 1, B works on Day 2 → 1 cycle = 2 days). Multiply the cycle to get as close to the total work as possible without exceeding it, and then assign the remaining work sequentially to the required person.
